Where Every Thread Tells a Story

We've been quietly working on a dream for a while now — and today, we'd like to show it to the people who matter most.

— Est. 2026 — Made by Hand — India to the World
A Letter from Saloni

What started as a quiet idea, became Dori.

For months, I've been deep in this — meeting our makers, sketching logos late at night, and obsessing over the way a knot lands on a piece of cotton. Today I'd like you to see what came of it.

The Urban Dori is my love letter to the artisans of India — to the women whose hands turn ordinary thread into pieces that make a house feel like home. Every basket, every bag, every small thing I make is rooted in their craft and finished with my care.

I'm sharing this with you first because you've been part of my journey in some way — friends, family, mentors, our circle. Take a look. Tell me what you think. And if a piece speaks to you, I'd love for it to live in your home.

Saloni Bajaj Founder, The Urban Dori
The Brand

The Urban Dori

Crafting homes that breathe with handmade warmth
and the timeless soul of Indian artistry.

Behind Every Knot

Hands that have woven for generations.

Our pieces don't come off a conveyor belt. They come from a sunlit workshop where artisans — most of them women — sit cross-legged on the floor, turning rope and yarn into the kind of things you want to keep forever.

We work directly with our partner ateliers — chosen with care, visited in person. We pay fairly. We honour the time it takes. And every order you place sends income straight back to the people who made it.
